name: ARC
ability_definition: The ability to combine pieces of information to form general rules or conclusions (includes finding a relationship among seemingly unrelated events).

task_realism.reasoning: In the workplace, inductive reasoning looks like diagnosing recurring equipment faults, spotting trends in sales or clinical data, forming hypotheses from case histories, or connecting seemingly unrelated incidents. ARC tasks are abstract colored-grid transformations with no domain semantics. They do exercise the core act of inferring a hidden rule from a few examples, but the content bears little resemblance to real work problems.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: ARC gives clean, noise-free, fully deterministic demonstrations and grades by exact match, with three attempts and offline compute limits. Real inductive work involves noisy and incomplete data, ambiguous or probabilistic rules, domain knowledge, tools, the chance to gather more evidence, and iterative feedback. The private set and novelty requirement do resemble real work in one way: they force generalization to unseen situations rather than recall.

construct_coverage.reasoning: ARC measures a central slice of the ability well: few-shot rule induction and application to new cases, under strong novelty. It leaves out much of the O*NET construct. It is limited to the visual-spatial grid domain. It excludes statistical and probabilistic generalization, causal inference from events, and linking information across heterogeneous sources ('relationship among seemingly unrelated events'). It also excludes judging how confident a conclusion should be when evidence is weak.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are small integer-colored grids, and outputs must be pixel-exact grids. These are toy artifacts, unlike the reports, datasets, logs, case notes, or written conclusions that inductive reasoning produces and consumes at work. The output format also rewards exact reproduction rather than a stated general rule or a justified conclusion.

transferability_reasoning: ARC is a construct-valid, contamination-resistant probe of pure few-shot rule induction, which makes it the best available isolate of the reasoning core. Its abstract grid domain, noise-free deterministic rules, and exact-match grid outputs are far removed from how inductive reasoning is used on noisy, semantically rich workplace information. Strong ARC performance signals a genuine underlying capacity, but it transfers only weakly and indirectly to real job tasks that require this ability.

2020.model_or_system: icecuber (Johan Sokrates Wind): brute-force program search over a hand-crafted DSL with 142 grid functions, composed in a DAG
2020.metric: percent of hidden private-test tasks solved (top-3 attempts allowed); equals 1 minus the official top-3 error of 0.794
2020.human_reference: General adult population. Inductive reasoning is a broad cognitive ability used across work settings. ARC was explicitly designed to need only core knowledge priors, not specialist training.

2021.model_or_system: icecuber (Johan Sokrates Wind), a brute-force program search over a domain-specific language of 142 hand-crafted grid functions
2021.metric: percent of tasks solved on the hidden private test set (accuracy, up to 3 attempts per task)
2021.human_reference: General adult population (typical adults doing novel few-shot rule induction)

2022.model_or_system: icecuber (Johan Sokrates Wind) DSL brute-force program search, 1st place Kaggle Abstraction and Reasoning Challenge 2020
2022.metric: percent of hidden private test tasks solved (top-3 exact match; the Kaggle metric was the error rate, ~0.794, i.e. about 20.6% solved)
2022.human_reference: General adult population. ARC requires only core-knowledge priors and no specialist training, so the typical working adult is the relevant population.

2023.model_or_system: Team SM (Somayyeh Gholami & Mehran Kazeminia) and Team MindsAI (Jack Cole), tied for first place in ARCathon 2023
2023.metric: percent of private evaluation tasks solved exactly (task accuracy, ARCathon protocol with three attempts per task)
2023.human_reference: General adult population (typical working adults doing novel few-shot rule induction; no specialist training is required for ARC)
